messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
A good rule‑of‑thumb for a typical U.S. home is **about 5 kWh of electricity per square foot per year**.  
Using that figure:

| Size | Annual kWh | Monthly kWh | Daily kWh |
|------|------------|-------------|-----------|
| 2 000 sq ft | ≈ 10 000 kWh | ≈ 833 kWh | ≈ 27 kWh |

So you’d expect roughly **10 000 kWh per year** (or about **833 kWh per month**, **27 kWh per day**) for a 2 000‑sq‑ft house.

> **Why this estimate?**  
> • The U.S. Energy Information Administration reports an average residential consumption of ~10 000 kWh per year.  
> • Dividing that by 2 000 sq ft gives ~5 kWh per sq ft per year, which is a common benchmark for modern, reasonably insulated homes.  

### Caveats & Variability

| Factor | Effect on Consumption |
|--------|-----------------------|
| Climate | Hot climates → more cooling; cold climates → more heating (electric heat). |
| Appliances | High‑efficiency vs. older appliances can change usage by ±10–20%. |
| Insulation & windows | Poor insulation can increase heating/cooling load by 10–30%. |
| Occupancy & habits | More occupants or heavy appliance use (e.g., electric ovens) can raise consumption. |
| Solar or wind generation | If you generate your own power, your grid draw will be lower. |

If you’re planning a solar system and want a more precise estimate of how many panels you’ll need, let me know and I can run the calculation for you.
